description.value: Sushi-Q is a Canadian chain founded in 1997 and one of the country's early pioneers of grab-and-go sushi, serving sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and Japanese ramen. The Burnaby outlet is located inside Lougheed Town Centre mall. The chain emphasises fresh daily preparation and chef-inspired presentation as its main differentiators.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Sushi-Q is an active Canadian sushi grab-and-go chain with a Burnaby outlet at Lougheed Town Centre. The website's location page lists this outlet as '#913K-9850 Austin Road, Burnaby, BC V3J 7B3', which differs from the OSM address (9855 Austin Road, V3J 1N4); the website value is used per the rules. The website describes the core model as 'grab-and-go' confirming takeout, and the menu lists a Veggie Combo plus multiple avocado/vegetable rolls confirming vegetarian options; no cyclist-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the site.
concerns: Address discrepancy: OSM lists '9855 Austin Road, Burnaby, V3J 1N4'; website location page lists this outlet as '#913K-9850 Austin Road, Burnaby, BC V3J 7B3' (Lougheed Town Centre). Street number, unit, and postal code all differ — OSM may have a data entry error.
No phone number is listed on the website for the Lougheed Town Centre (Burnaby) outlet, and OSM has no phone either.
Website OSM name is 'Sushi Q' but the website consistently uses the hyphenated form 'Sushi-Q'.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly accessible grab-and-go restaurant inside a major mall; a useful stop for touring cyclists seeking a quick meal.
enrichment_extras.notes: Mall food-court location inside Lougheed Town Centre; mall washrooms and covered bicycle parking near mall entrances are plausible but not confirmed from available evidence.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu includes Veggie Combo, Avocado Roll Plus, Avocado Maki Plus, Kappa Maki Plus, Avocado Cucumber Plus, and Seaweed Salad — multiple vegetarian options confirmed

wow_evidence: Canadian chain founded in 1997... one of the country's early pioneers of grab-and-go sushi
